capabilities: Browse 115 folders in a sidebar tree with breadcrumbs, name search and quota bar
Sign in to 115 by scanning a QR code in settings
Serve 115 read and write tools over a local MCP endpoint guarded by a token header
Enforce a hard-coded safety policy: single-item requests, quarantine before delete, write rate limits, audit log
Run an opt-in vault backup through a local Python helper script
disambiguation: Not a general MCP server host; it only exposes 115 cloud drive tools from its own local endpoint.
extras: Desktop only. Write tools are off by default and stay disabled until read-only browsing works. The plugin listens on 127.0.0.1 and requires an x-115-token header on every request; the 115 cookie is kept in the plugin's data.json and audit logs go to the plugin's data/ subfolder. The optional backup feature needs filesystem and process access to spawn a user-configured Python interpreter and script path, and shares a cross-process lock file with the Python batch scripts that can live outside the vault. Not yet in the community directory ("once approved"). README is bilingual English/Chinese.
problem: Managing files on a 115 cloud drive normally means leaving Obsidian for a web or mobile client, and letting an agent touch that drive risks uncontrolled batch deletions.

requires.name: 115 cloud drive account and mobile app for QR login

summary: Sidebar file browser for a 115 cloud drive that also exposes token-protected 115 read/write tools to agents over a local MCP endpoint.
